title: Copy phase from blank tapes
statement: Let $C$ be a finite binary Turing machine with at least one work tape, let $entry,exit$ be states of $C$, and let $x$ be a binary word. For any $i\in\mathbb{N}$ with $i\le |x|$, the wrapper machine started on $x$ reaches after $i$ steps a copy-phase configuration with input head at position $i+1$, tape zero containing the prefix of $x$ of length $i$, and its head at position $i$; all other work tapes and heads are blank and at zero, respectively, and the output is empty.
hypotheses_covered: $C$ has at least one work tape
replaced:
For every $i \le |x|$, running the decider wrapper for $i$ steps from its
initial configuration on $x$ reaches the copy-phase configuration with the first
$i$ input bits on tape zero and both active heads just past them.
